## noisefloor: propose starter saturation rule for `search`

`search` carries no alert coverage on **saturation** at all -- confirmed by `noisefloor coverage`, which found no rule anywhere in this checkout whose expression names this service on this signal. This proposes a first, minimal starter rule to close that gap.

> [!WARNING]
> **The gap above is measured. The threshold below is not.** Every other proposal noisefloor opens (a retire or a tune) states a number derived from thirty days of a rule's own firing history. This rule has never existed, so there is no history to derive a threshold from -- it is a conservative starting point, not a recommendation. Expect to tune it after it has run for a while.

| what | value | measured? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| traffic proxy | 40.12 req/s | yes -- this is why the service was ranked as a blind spot worth acting on |
| selector used | `job="search"` | -- |
| proposed `for:` | 15m | no -- a fixed template default |
| proposed threshold | see expression below | **partially** -- scaled from this service's own current reading, see below |

**Where the threshold comes from:** this service's own current process_resident_memory_bytes reading is 540MB; the threshold below is 1.5x that (810MB).

**Proposed rule** (appended to group `services` in `testdata/starter_fixture.yml`):

```yaml
- alert: SearchMemoryHigh
  expr: sum(process_resident_memory_bytes{job="search"}) > 810000000
  for: 15m
  labels: {severity: warning}
  annotations: {summary: "search resident memory above 810MB"}
```

**How to check this**

Run the metric this rule reads against your own Prometheus and confirm it exists and looks the way this body claims:

    process_resident_memory_bytes{job="search"}

noisefloor verified this metric exists for `search` before proposing this rule; it does not verify that the THRESHOLD is right for your traffic pattern, because nothing could -- that is what tuning this rule after it has run for a while is for.

---
Generated by noisefloor from a coverage scan, not from firing history: there is none yet for a rule that has never existed. Review the threshold before merging, and revisit it with `noisefloor scan` once this rule has run for a while.
